strings.Tool use: the chat template supports too: Tool use: the chat template supports tool_calls
strings.Prompt processing (PP): llama.cpp's nati: Prompt processing (PP): llama.cpp's native prompt_per_second timing after an excluded warm-up (or prompt_n / prompt_ms when the direct field is unavailable). The deterministic prompt uses each run's saved context fraction. Only Standard is capped at 65,536 prompt tokens; Custom is uncapped. Prompt caching is disabled.
strings.n_decode: llama.cpp's native predicted_p: n_decode: llama.cpp's native predicted_per_second timing (or predicted_n / predicted_ms fallback). AutoTuner requests 256 deterministic decode tokens with EOS ignored and uses the median of the accepted samples.
strings.End-to-end: (prompt tokens + generated t: End-to-end: (prompt tokens + generated tokens) divided by native prompt time plus native decode time for this exact workload. This is the score used to rank candidates and performance modes.
strings.Selects which llama.cpp build starts the: Selects which llama.cpp build starts the server. AutoTuner can choose a more compatible build for a specific model when needed.
strings.The selected directory supplies llama-se: The selected directory supplies llama-server or the matching diffusion binary. Model YAML profiles may override this default for required forks or features. Build discovery scans the enabled llama.cpp roots configured with the adjacent llama Builds button.
strings.Conservative. KV reserved for 128k (MoE): Conservative. KV reserved for 128k (MoE) / 64k (dense) context, generous safety bands. Single slot with the full context. Pick this for long-context sessions.
strings.Default. KV reserved for 64k (MoE) / 32k: Default. KV reserved for 64k (MoE) / 32k (dense) context — enough headroom for most chats while letting more weight/expert layers fit on GPU. Single slot.
strings.Aggressive. KV reserved for only 32k (Mo: Aggressive. KV reserved for only 32k (MoE) / 16k (dense) — every spare GB of VRAM goes to weight/expert layers for max tokens/s. Single slot. Not recommended for very long context.
strings.Max context for low-VRAM / high-RAM syst: Max context for low-VRAM / high-RAM systems (e.g. 8 GB VRAM, 64 GB RAM). KV cache moves to system RAM (--no-kv-offload), trading generation speed for far larger context — the only way to reach 90k+ on a 20 GB MoE that barely fits the GPU. Single parallel slot.

profile_notes._default.yaml: Fallback profile. It is used whenever no specific profile matches. Chat defaults are deliberately conservative (temp 0.7); coding is clearly more deterministic (temp 0.2). Model-specific YAML files override this.
profile_notes.agents-a1.yaml: Agents-A1 (InternScience, 2026, Apache 2.0) is a 35B-A3B MoE agent model post-trained on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (GGUF architecture "qwen35moe", hybrid GatedDeltaNet + full attention; the scanner counts the KV cache correctly through recurrent_layers). This profile matches only by the filename pattern ("agents-a1"); re-quants without that name correctly fall back to the qwen3_5-3_6 architecture fallback. Native 256k context (YaRN up to ~1M). Sampling uses the official card values temp=0.85 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 / rep=1.0; presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of the official 1.1 because presence_penalty reproducibly causes loops during tool calling (see qwen3_5-3_6.yaml); for pure chat use: -- --presence-penalty 1.1. Reasoning model (<think> blocks, Qwen3 parser) with native function calling. Tip: `--jinja` at start cleanly separates <think> into the reasoning_content field and parses <tool_call> blocks as OpenAI-style tool_calls: -- --jinja. CAUTION when downloading: InternScience/Agents-A1 itself is Safetensors; use the GGUF repositories for the tuner (for example InternScience/Agents-A1-Q4_K_M-GGUF or LordNeel/Agents-A1-GGUF). A current llama.cpp mainline with qwen35moe support is required (b9963 is fine).
profile_notes.bailingmoe2-5.yaml: InclusionAI (Ant Group) Ling-2.6-flash is a MoE with hybrid attention, architecture "bailingmoe2.5" / "bailing_hybrid". CAUTION (as of b9739): NOT in vanilla llama.cpp; it needs a Ling-2.6-capable fork (for example ik_llama.cpp). Select that fork in the GUI's fork dropdown; the GGUF already declares the architecture and will run on mainline without re-downloading once BailingMoeV2.5 is merged there. Normal autoregressive server model. Sampling follows the InclusionAI recommendation temp=0.7 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05; coding is more deterministic. --jinja for template/reasoning. Ling/Ring 2.0 ("bailingmoe2", mainline) is handled by ling-ring.yaml.
profile_notes.bonsai-27b.yaml: PrismML Bonsai 27B on a Qwen3.6-27B base: multimodal, thinking- and tool-calling-capable, 262k native context. The Q1_0-g128 language weights take about 3.9 GB; the optional vision projector takes another roughly 0.63 GB. Current mainline llama.cpp supports Q1_0 on CPU, Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan. PrismML's Q4_0 KV cache saves considerable memory at very long context but is not a speed feature.
profile_notes.bonsai-ternary-27b.yaml: PrismML Ternary-Bonsai 27B on a Qwen3.6-27B base: multimodal, thinking- and tool-calling-capable, 262k native context. The Q2_0-g128 weights ({-1, 0, +1}) take about 7.2 GB; the optional vision projector another roughly 0.63 GB. Use the PrismML prism fork for the published Q2_0-g128 file. The separate Q2_0_g64 file is intended for current mainline llama.cpp (currently CPU/Metal; further backends follow).
profile_notes.bonsai-ternary.yaml: Ternary-Bonsai (8B/4B/1.7B): weights in {-1, 0, +1} (1.58 bits per weight). Between 1-bit Bonsai and full precision: about 9x smaller, 5x faster, and better on benchmarks than 1-bit Bonsai (avg +5 points). Q2_0 is the storage format used (2-bit aligned for Metal/CUDA). Requires the PrismML 2b_llama.cpp fork (ternary kernels, 2-bit Q2_0).
profile_notes.bonsai.yaml: PrismML Bonsai 8B is the first commercially viable 1-bit LLM (Q1_0 GGUF, ~1.15 GB). Competitive with full-precision 8B models while 14x smaller and 8x faster on edge hardware. Requires the PrismML fork of llama.cpp (1b_llama.cpp), not mainline. The Q1_0 quant is merged upstream for CPU/Metal/CUDA/Vulkan, but AMD ROCm and the optimised x86 paths still need the fork. The coding profile is only slightly lowered (0.3) instead of an aggressive 0.15: at extremely low temperatures 1-bit quants tend to loop.
profile_notes.cohere2moe.yaml: Cohere North-Mini-Code-1.0: 30B total / 3B active MoE for agentic coding (tool use, repository tasks, browser automation), Apache-2.0, architecture "cohere2moe" (cohere2 iSWA attention + glm4moe-style sigmoid gating, 1 leading dense + 48 MoE layers, 128 experts / 8 active). NOTE: cohere2moe has been in llama.cpp mainline since b9626 (PR #24260), so on b9829 it runs without a fork or PR branch; only builds before b9626 still need the PR branch. Normal autoregressive server model (no diffusion path). Sampling follows the Cohere/Unsloth recommendation (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95) in chat; the coding profile is more deterministic (0.6) for stable tool calls. --jinja is mandatory (chat template + tool parsing).
profile_notes.cohere_command_r.yaml: Specialised in RAG and tool calling. Low temperature already in chat mode because Command R/R+ is meant to cite from sources: "chat" here is document-grounded conversation rather than free writing. The coding profile is almost greedy (0.1) for deterministic tool calls and structured output.
profile_notes.deepseek-ocr.yaml: DeepSeek-OCR v1/v2 document model. The verified prompt is "Free OCR."; Unlimited-OCR is a distinct checkpoint with the same GGUF architecture and uses its own name-matched profile and "document parsing." prompt.
profile_notes.deepseek-r1-v3.yaml: DeepSeek-V3.2 (671B MoE / 37B active) with DSA for efficient long-context attention, or R1 (reasoning). The R1 and V3.2 models use <think> tags for chain-of-thought. The coding profile uses temp=0.3 (vs. 1.0 chat) for more deterministic final code while the reasoning chain stays "creative". CAUTION: the Speciale variant (V3.2-Speciale) does NOT support tool calling.
profile_notes.deepseek-v4.yaml: DeepSeek-V4 Pro (1.6T-A49B) and Flash (284B-A13B) are 1M-context MoE models with the dedicated deepseek4 GGUF architecture. Base architecture support started earlier, but this combined Pro/Flash profile requires llama.cpp b10254+ for the dedicated V4-Flash chat-template contract; a current build is strongly preferred for later backend/indexer and KV fixes. Official decoding defaults are temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0. Think-Max workflows should reserve at least a 384k context window. These are datacenter-scale models; local workstation use needs very aggressive quantization plus large system RAM and CPU expert offload. Keep preserved reasoning for long agent/tool sessions. llama.cpp b10786 adds the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp projector (deepseek4v mmproj) and the image-token routing bias; vision needs that build plus a matching mmproj file, and image spans attend bidirectionally inside the sliding window.
profile_notes.devstral.yaml: Optimised for code completion (Cline, Aider, VS Code). The coding profile (temp=0.15) gives deterministic completion; the chat profile (temp=0.4) suits code explanations and discussion.
profile_notes.diffusion-gemma.yaml: DiffusionGemma is a diffusion text model (not an autoregressive GGUF for the normal llama-server). It runs through llama-diffusion-gemma-server (PR #24427), a SEPARATE OpenAI-compatible HTTP server with /health, /v1/chat/completions, /props, and port binding. Select your diffusion build in the GUI's fork dropdown (for example "d_bXXXX_vulkan_llama.cpp" or "d_bXXXX_hip_llama.cpp"); AutoTuner finds llama-diffusion-gemma-server inside it automatically, no path needs to be hard-coded. The server stays queryable (chat UI, RooCode, OpenAI clients); port and state behave like any other server. Mainline b9700 does not recognise the "diffusion-gemma" architecture; AutoTuner still detects it (is_diffusion) and automatically selects the gemma-server runner. Mainline diffusion models (Dream/LLaDA/RND1) have NO server of their own and instead run single-shot through llama-diffusion-cli. Scheduling: EITHER --diffusion-eps OR --diffusion-block-length, not both (DiffusionGemma uses block scheduling). Fork-specific flags must be enabled through diffusion.fork_args if your build knows them. IMPORTANT for VRAM: DiffusionGemma has an extremely large F16 KV cache (k/v_length=512, 5x normal). Auto is therefore capped at 4096 (KV ~0.47 GiB); 8192 can, with allocator overhead, reach a contiguous 1 GiB Vulkan allocation and crash despite free total VRAM. The calculation also reserves 1.5 GiB of diffusion runtime overhead. Pinning to the 32 GB R9700 happens automatically (env_overrides).
profile_notes.dots1.yaml: rednote-hilab dots.llm1: MoE, 142B total / 14B active (Instruct + Base), architecture "dots1", native 32k context, performance at Qwen2.5-72B level. rednote's card gives no explicit sampler recommendation, so conservative middle-of-the-road defaults are used (temp 0.7 chat / 0.3 coding); adjust to the generation_config if needed. With only 14B active parameters plus --n-cpu-moe it runs well on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.ernie-4_5.yaml: Baidu ERNIE 4.5: MoE family, Apache-2.0, architecture "ernie4_5-moe". Variants: 300B-A47B (datacenter/cluster) and 21B-A3B (local, also as a Thinking edition), native context up to 131072. Sampling is conservative (temp 0.8 / top_p 0.8 chat, 0.6 coding) because Baidu publishes no prominent unified llama.cpp recommendation; adjust to the generation_config of the specific variant if needed. --jinja for the chat template / thinking separation. 21B-A3B (3B active) runs well with --n-cpu-moe on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.exaone-4_5.yaml: LG AI Research EXAONE 4.5: LG's first open-weight VLM, 33B total (31.7B core + 1.29B vision), DENSE, text+image, 256k context. Hybrid attention (3x SWA-4096 + 1x global NoPE, 16x), 64 layers. IMPORTANT licence: non-commercial, research/academic only, no production use (unlike most other profiles here). LG's launch command uses `-fa on -sm row -c 262144 --no-context-shift`; `-sm row` (row split) instead of layer split can be more stable on multi-GPU with this hybrid attention; apply via the Expert panel / extra args if needed. Vision needs the separate mmproj file (mmproj-EXAONE-4.5-*.gguf). Integrated MTP/NextN layers exist in the GGUF but are NOT executed by llama.cpp (b9500), so no draft-mtp; draftless ngram-mod is used instead. presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of LG's official 1.5 because 1.5 causes loops in tool calling / structured output; for pure chat without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`.
profile_notes.frankenmerger.yaml: Merges often have inconsistent context limits and sampling sweet spots. The chat profile is optimised for roleplay/creative writing (higher temperature, stronger repeat penalty against loops in long RP sessions). The coding profile is defensive: these models are not primarily trained for code; if code performance is poor, prefer a dedicated coder profile.
profile_notes.gemma-3.yaml: Google's Gemma 3 family. The 1B model is text-only with 32k context; 4B/12B/27B support text and image input with 128k context. AutoTuner uses the GGUF context metadata to distinguish the 1B limit and attaches a matching sibling mmproj when present. Official instruction-tuned sampling is temp 1.0, top_k 64, top_p 0.95, with repetition penalty left at 1.0.
profile_notes.gemma-3n.yaml: Gemma 3n E2B/E4B has a native 32k context and official temp 1.0, top_k 64, top_p 0.95 sampling. llama.cpp b10760 supports its text and vision paths, but the MTMD code still intentionally skips Gemma 3n audio tensors; do not present a current stock build as local audio-capable. A matching sibling mmproj is attached automatically when available.
profile_notes.gemma-4.yaml: Gemma is sensitive to repeat_penalty > 1.0. Multimodality by size: E2B/E4B = text+image+audio, 12B = text+image+audio (NEW "Unified" variant: encoder-free, vision/audio through direct linear projections instead of separate encoders), 26B-A4B + 31B = text+image. Context: E2B/E4B = 128k, 12B/26B-A4B/31B = 256k. Architecture note: the 12B language-model GGUF loads under general.architecture "gemma4" (identical to the rest of the family); the strings gemma4uv/gemma4ua are only projector types on the separate mmproj file. Scanner, KV logic, and match_profile therefore treat the 12B like any other Gemma 4 model. Thinking mode can be enabled with <|think|> at the start of the system prompt. The coding profile uses temp=1.5 (vs. 1.0 chat) following community tests showing that Gemma 4 produces more creative and more correct coding solutions at a higher temperature; override with `-- --temp 1.0` if the higher temperature disturbs your workflow. The sampler order is set explicitly through extra_args as "temperature;top_p;top_k" (Gemma 4 recommendation; see the comment above), which matters because the default sampler chain would otherwise distort the high coding temperature.
profile_notes.glm-4_7.yaml: Flagship 358B MoE coding model or the 30B Flash variant. Three-level thinking architecture (interleaved / preserved / turn-level thinking). Very strong in SWE-Bench (~73.8% for the full model, 59.2% for Flash) and tool use. The chat profile is Z.ai's official "general evaluation" recommendation (temp 1.0). The coding profile is more deterministic (0.6) for stable tool calls and reproducible code output. Note: GLM-5.1 (Z.ai's newest coding model, 256k context) now exists as well and will eventually need its own profile. Tip: set `thinking=enabled` for coding; internal reasoning traces noticeably improve code quality.
profile_notes.glm-5.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5/5.1 is a 744B-A40B MoE family for agentic coding and reasoning, with roughly 200k native context. Official chat sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95; coding uses the established deterministic temp 0.6 local profile. --jinja and preserved reasoning are important for long tool workflows. GLM-5.2 is intentionally separate because it adds a 1M context, glm-dsa/IndexShare attention, an improved MTP layer, and a newer minimum llama.cpp build.
profile_notes.glm-5_2.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (non-Flash) share the glm-dsa GGUF architecture, native 1M context, IndexShare sparse attention, and one NextN/MTP layer, so they intentionally share this profile. GLM-5.3 keeps the official generation config temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 and adds low/high/max reasoning effort in its embedded template (max by default); min_p=0.01 and top_k=40 retain the established local profile. Use llama.cpp b10174 or newer for the complete GLM DSA/MTP path, with current builds strongly preferred for indexer/backend fixes. Datacenter scale: even low-bit quants need hundreds of GB, so a 48 GB workstation requires substantial RAM/CPU expert offload and cannot exploit a 1M cache. GLM-5.3-Flash is intentionally separate: it is a 320B-A18B multimodal KDA/DSA hybrid with the new glm5next architecture.
profile_notes.glm-5_3_flash.yaml: Z.ai GLM-5.3-Flash is a natively multimodal 320B-A18B MoE with 45 layers: 34 KDA linear-attention layers plus 11 pooled DSA/MLA layers, mHC residual streams, 288 routed experts (top-8) + 1 shared expert, one NextN/MTP layer, and native 1M context. Official sampling is temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95; the embedded template supports low/high/max reasoning effort and defaults to max. IMPORTANT: as of 2026-08-30, glm5next support is still in open upstream llama.cpp PRs #27752 (text + experimental MTP) and #27773 (text + vision); stock mainline does not load the architecture yet. Use a matching patched build and GGUF conversion. The implementations have different current trade-offs: one omits vision, the other keeps MTP for a separate PR, and multiple sequences require unified KV handling. Published Unsloth GGUFs use general.architecture=glm5next and offer separate mmproj files. Prefer IQ3 or higher: real Metal/CPU testing reported repeated-token failure for UD-IQ1_M while IQ3_XXS and IQ4_XS remained coherent. Current development CUDA also has a reported DSA-pool ceiling near 262k context, so AutoTuner caps this preview profile at 262,140 despite the model's native 1M metadata. Raise that cap only after the selected runtime fixes and validates the full window.
profile_notes.gpt-oss.yaml: OpenAI gpt-oss (20B: 21B total / 3.6B active; 120B: 117B / 5.1B active), architecture "gpt-oss", native MXFP4 MoE (in llama.cpp mainline). The 20B runs in 16 GB VRAM. MUST be run with the harmony format: `--jinja` is mandatory here, otherwise the output is garbled. Sampling is deliberately unusual (temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / NO top_k / NO repeat_penalty): top_k and penalties truncate or break the harmony control tokens and destroy the chain-of-thought. Reasoning effort is NOT controlled by a sampler but through the system prompt ("Reasoning: low|medium|high"); in the AutoTuner GUI it can be set per model as reasoning_effort (low/medium/high), which llama-server passes through via `--chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'`. The full chain-of-thought is visible through the API but, according to OpenAI, NOT intended for end users. Native tool/function-calling capabilities are present. Quant levels change almost nothing about the file size of the MXFP4 MoE: the experts are always MXFP4; q8_0/F16 only affect embeddings/attention.
profile_notes.granite-4_1.yaml: Dense decoder-only Transformer (3B/8B/30B), not a reasoning model. Strong in tool calling, instruction following, RAG, and coding. The 3B checkpoint supports 128k context; 8B and 30B support up to 512k. Granite Switch 4.1 is intentionally separate because it uses the dedicated graniteswitch architecture and requires a newer llama.cpp build. Apache 2.0 license. Do not use CUDA 13.2 because it can produce gibberish; this warning does not affect Vulkan on AMD.
profile_notes.granite-4_2.yaml: IBM Granite 4.2 is a dense 3B/8B/30B reasoning family with default full thinking, optional non-thinking and low-effort modes, reasoning-augmented tool calling, coding, and multilingual chat. The embedded Jinja template accepts enable_thinking, low_effort, and reasoning_effort=low; AutoTuner's Expert reasoning controls can pass the matching template kwargs. All three checkpoints are natively 128k. IBM advertises a 512k long-context extension only for 30B, while its published serving commands and checkpoint config use 131,072; this profile therefore keeps the safe native limit. Apache 2.0.
profile_notes.granite-embedding-r2.yaml: IBM Granite Embedding Multilingual R2 (April 2026): ModernBERT-based dense embedding models, architecture "modern-bert". Two sizes: 97m (384-dim) and 311m (768-dim, Matryoshka 768->512/384/256/128). 200+ languages (extended for 52 + code), 32768-token context, CLS pooling, Apache 2.0. NO chat/completion: run it as an embedding endpoint (--embeddings and --pooling cls are set in extra_args). Use cases: semantic search, RAG retrieval. The reranker is a separate model. NOTE: if AutoTuner GUI logic (sampling dropdowns, draft/n-gram checkboxes, KV quant) remains visible for this profile, simply ignore it; in --embeddings mode it has no effect. Should a future AutoTuner build gain an explicit "embedding" task switch, this profile can be simplified accordingly.
profile_notes.granite-switch-4_1.yaml: IBM Granite Switch 4.1 uses embedded adapters selected by control tokens for RAG, safety, and explainability workloads. It has a dedicated graniteswitch GGUF architecture and 128k context. Use llama.cpp b10342 or newer. Chat keeps modest variation; coding/tool workflows use IBM-style greedy decoding. Apache 2.0 license.
profile_notes.grok.yaml: xAI Grok-2: large MoE, open weights, architecture "grok" (in llama.cpp mainline). Native context up to 131072. xAI gives no prominent llama.cpp sampler recommendation, so conservative defaults are used (temp 0.7 chat / 0.3 coding); adjust if needed. Datacenter/cluster class (several hundred GB depending on quant); on a single workstation only with a lot of RAM plus --n-cpu-moe.
profile_notes.hunyuan-moe.yaml: Tencent Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct: fine-grained MoE, 80B total / 13B active, architecture "hunyuan_moe" (NOT "hunyuan-dense"!). Hybrid reasoning (fast/slow thinking, dynamic CoT depth), native 256k context. Sampling uses Tencent's official CHAT values temp=0.7 / top_k=20 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05, deliberately separated from the Hunyuan-MT translator profile (top_p 0.6), which would be wrong for an A13B chat model. --jinja is mandatory. With 13B active parameters it runs well on a 32 GB card plus --n-cpu-moe. Note: some early GGUF quants had a broken, very high perplexity; prefer verified quants (for example Unsloth Dynamic).
profile_notes.hunyuan.yaml: Tencent Hunyuan-MT (HY-MT2-7B): dense 7B translation model, architecture "hunyuan-dense" (supported in llama.cpp mainline, no mmproj, no hybrid). The sampling defaults are Tencent's official Hunyuan-MT values (temp 0.7 / top_p 0.6 / top_k 20 / rep 1.05), deliberately different from the usual chat profiles because the model is trained for translation rather than free writing. NOTE: should this profile later also catch generic Hunyuan CHAT models (for example Hunyuan-A13B), temp 1.0 would be more appropriate there; create a separate profile with a more specific pattern in that case. general.name shows a checkpoint name ("Global_Step_560") for this GGUF; that is cosmetic and does not affect loading.
profile_notes.hy-mt2.yaml: Tencent Hy-MT2 (May 2026): "fast-thinking" translation family (33 languages): 1.8B / 7B dense, 30B-A3B MoE (30B total / 3B active). The architecture is NEW: general.architecture "hy_v3", not compatible with the old Hunyuan-MT profile (hunyuan-dense) or A13B (hunyuan_moe). Since llama.cpp b9993 (PR #25395) hy_v3 including MTP support is part of mainline. The 1.8B/7B GGUFs with architecture "hunyuan-dense" already ran before that. Sampling uses the official Tencent values temp=0.7 / top_p=1.0 / top_k off / rep=1.0, deliberately different from the old Hunyuan-MT (top_p 0.6). Coding mode is greedy (temp 0) for reproducible, literal translations. Pure translation model, not a chat/coding LLM. Note from the GGUF repository (litigerking): with llama-cli you may need -r '<eos:6124c78e>' as a reverse prompt for clean EOS handling; not needed for the tuner's llama-server path.
profile_notes.hy4-preview.yaml: Tencent Hy4 Preview (August 2026): 770B total / 49B active MoE, 78 layers, 256 routed experts + 1 shared expert, top-8 routing, Gated DSA/IndexCache, iHC residual streams, and native 1M context. Official sampling is temp=0.9, top_p=1.0, top_k disabled; reasoning defaults to high and can be changed by the embedded chat template's reasoning_effort parameter. IMPORTANT: stock upstream llama.cpp does not yet contain the "hyv4" architecture at the time of this profile. AngelSlim/Hy4-preview-GGUF documents a community patch based on llama.cpp commit 0cea36222; both published GGUFs require that architecture patch. Their Q4_K_M is about 435 GiB and STQ1_0 about 214 GiB at full residency, so practical use needs datacenter-class aggregate VRAM or very large RAM with expert offload. The community conversion drops Hy4's native MTP layer, therefore its GGUF cannot use embedded speculative decoding.
profile_notes.kimi-k2.yaml: Moonshot Kimi-K2: 1T total / 32B active MoE with MLA, architecture "deepseek2" (DeepSeek-V3-like). Therefore NO arch_fallback: it would otherwise also catch DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 and GLM-4.7-Flash; matching only through the filename "kimi". Variants: K2-Instruct(-0905, text), K2.5/K2.6 (vision via mmproj, merged in mainline), K2.7-Code. Sampling: chat = Moonshot/Unsloth temp=0.6 / min_p=0.01 (against repetition); coding = thinking defaults temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 (K2.5+/K2.7 use thinking; "instant" is not supported there). --jinja is mandatory (tool calls). Datacenter class: Q2 ~250-380 GB, Q4 ~620 GB; a cluster or a workstation with a very large amount of RAM. Note: some ubergarm/ik quants need the ik_llama.cpp fork; the standard Unsloth/bartowski quants run on mainline.
profile_notes.kimi-k3.yaml: Moonshot Kimi-K3 is a native-multimodal 2.8T-A104B MoE with KDA, Attention Residuals, 896 experts (16 active), and 1M context. llama.cpp b10448 added the dedicated kimi-k3 TEXT loader and converter; its converter deliberately skips vision_tower/mm_projector tensors, so current mainline support must not be presented as local K3 vision support. K3 cannot be routed through the older kimi-linear or Kimi-K2/deepseek2 loaders. Official settings use temp 1.0 with top_p 0.95 for single-step work and 1.0 for agentic tasks. The profile requires b10749 because that is the first tagged build with corrected no-scan SSM state tensors for Kimi-K3/Kimi-Linear. Thinking stays enabled and complete reasoning/tool-call history is preserved. At this scale it remains a cluster or very-high-RAM model, not a practical 48 GB workstation checkpoint.
profile_notes.kimi-linear.yaml: Moonshot's 48B-A3B hybrid model uses three KDA layers for every global MLA layer and supports a 1M context with a much smaller recurrent-state footprint. Mainline architecture support began at b7957, but b10749 is required here for the corrected no-scan treatment of Kimi Linear SSM state tensors; older builds can silently use the wrong allocation/lifetime contract. This profile is separate from Kimi-K2 (deepseek2) and Kimi-K3 (kimi-k3). The official model card does not prescribe temperature/top-k/top-p, so embedded GGUF sampling metadata remains authoritative when present.
profile_notes.laguna-s-2_1.yaml: Laguna S 2.1 (Poolside) is a text-only 117.6B-A8.5B MoE built for long-horizon agentic coding, terminal work, tool use, and preserved interleaved reasoning. Use llama.cpp b10087 or newer for the Unsloth GGUF; for sharded Unsloth quants select only shard 00001 and llama.cpp loads the remaining shards automatically. The native context is 1M; GGUF metadata already carries YaRN factor 128 with original context 8192, so no manual RoPE override is required. Thinking is enabled by the embedded template by default. For quick replies it can be disabled per request with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking":false}. Keep reasoning history for coding agents. Optional official Laguna-S-2.1-DFlash-BF16.gguf (~2.2 GB) enables DFlash speculation; leave it unassigned if VRAM pressure or Vulkan benchmarks show no speedup.
profile_notes.leanstral.yaml: Leanstral 1.5 (Mistral, 3 July 2026): Apache-2.0 Lean 4 code-agent and theorem-proving model. Sparse MoE: 119B total / 6.5B active (A6B), 128 experts, 4 active per token, MLA attention (DeepSeek style), 256k context, multimodal input (text+image; optionally load the matching mmproj file and assign it as mmproj in the GUI; without mmproj only the text path runs). Trained with CISPO RL in a multi-turn proof environment (Lean compiler feedback) and a code-agent environment (filesystem + Lean LSP). Saturates miniF2F, solves 587/672 PutnamBench, SOTA on FATE-H. Chat profile = high-reasoning/proof mode (temp 0.7), coding profile = deterministic code agent (temp 0.2). Set reasoning mode explicitly: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'. NOTE on test-time scaling: Leanstral scales monotonically with the token budget (244 solved problems at 200k -> 587 at 4M on PutnamBench). For pass@k proof search (sampling many proof candidates) it pays to raise the temperature towards 1.0 to generate diverse proof paths; in chat mode via -- --temp 1.0. Vibe CLI (Mistral): vibe --agent lean.
profile_notes.lfm2.yaml: LiquidAI LFM2 / LFM2.5 edge family (short conv + GQA). Sampling follows LiquidAI's official recommendation (temp 0.3, min_p 0.15, rep 1.05): small models, hence a deliberately low temperature against incoherence. IMPORTANT (LFM2.5-Audio): this is an audio-in/audio-out speech model. This profile only provides sensible text-side defaults; the actual audio pipeline (audio encoder/decoder) runs through the dedicated llama.cpp audio paths, not through the plain text chat server. Loaded as a text chat model it works but produces no speech. LFM2 is technically a conv/attention hybrid; for this 1.5B model the tuner's KV-cache overestimate is negligible (tiny model).
profile_notes.ling-3.yaml: InclusionAI Ling 3.0 uses the bailingmoe3 hybrid KDA/MLA MoE architecture. Flash is 124B-A5.1B with 256k context; Tiny is the smaller 7.9B-A1.3B sibling. Official sampling is temp 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 with thinking enabled. llama.cpp b10460 added conversion, inference, integrated and separate NEXTN/MTP support; this profile requires b10749 because that is the first tagged build with corrected no-scan BailingMoE3 SSM state tensors. Compatible MTP weights can use up to three speculative tokens. Do not route these checkpoints through the older Ling 2.6 bailingmoe2.5/bailing_hybrid fork profile.
profile_notes.ling-ring.yaml: InclusionAI (Ant Group) Ling / Ring 2.x: MoE family, architecture "bailingmoe2" (mainline via PR #16063). Ling = instruct/general, Ring = reasoning (derived from Ling, <think> chains). Sizes: Ling/Ring-mini-2.0 (~17B / 1.4B active, runs well locally), -flash, and the 1T flagships (Ling-2.5-1T / Ring-1T, 1T total / ~63B active, hybrid linear attention, up to 1M context; pure datacenter/cluster models, Q4 ~500 GB). Sampling follows the InclusionAI recommendation temp=0.7 / top_p=0.8 / rep=1.05; coding is more deterministic. --jinja for template/reasoning. IMPORTANT: Ling-2.6-flash uses the newer "bailingmoe2.5" and does NOT run on vanilla llama.cpp; use bailingmoe2-5.yaml (fork) for it.
profile_notes.llama-3.yaml: Standard profile for Meta's Llama 3 series. Llama 3.1+ natively supports 128k context; older and smaller variants are limited to their real limit through GGUF metadata. Llama 4 has its own profile because of its different official sampling and 1M/10M context limits. Chat is the all-round default; coding is strongly deterministic.
profile_notes.llama-4.yaml: Meta's multimodal Llama 4 MoE family. Official Instruct limits are 10M for Scout and 1M for Maverick; base checkpoints are 256k. AutoTuner always caps this family maximum with each GGUF's native context metadata and the actual RAM/VRAM budget, so Maverick is never promoted to Scout's limit. Official reference generation defaults are temp 0.6 / top_p 0.9. Image input needs a matching mmproj; llama.cpp b10760 still warns that Llama 4 vision quality is known to be degraded, so validate vision-critical workloads independently.
profile_notes.mellum.yaml: JetBrains Mellum2-12B-A2.5B: sparse MoE (64 experts, 8 active), 12B total / 2.5B active, 128k context via layer-selective YaRN, Apache 2.0. No multimodality. Inference cost/speed behaves like a dense 2.5B despite the 12B total size. Three variants: Base (completion), Instruct (direct), Thinking (<think> CoT). For the Thinking variant set `--jinja` as an extra arg so that <think> blocks are cleanly separated into the reasoning_content field: -- --jinja. ngram_method is DELIBERATELY set to ngram-map-k4v here (not the global default ngram-mod): it is MTP-compatible and survives both cases, whether or not llama.cpp recognises/executes the MTP head JetBrains describes. On crashes with speculation: disable draft/n-gram in the GUI and compare tok/s (a MoE A2.5B does not benefit from speculation for certain).
profile_notes.microsoft_phi-4-3_5.yaml: Small but extremely capable model. Runs most stably with greedy decoding (temp 0) for logical tasks, which is therefore the coding default. Chat mode allows some variation (temp 0.5) but stays clearly more conservative than with larger models because Phi hallucinates faster at high temperature than 30B+ models.
profile_notes.minicpm5.yaml: OpenBMB MiniCPM5-1B: dense 1B on-device model (standard llama architecture, no hybrid, no mmproj), Apache-2.0, 1B-class SOTA for tool use/code/reasoning, native 128k context. Architecture "llama", therefore NO arch_fallback (it would otherwise catch all Llama models); matching only by filename. Hybrid reasoning from one checkpoint: think/no-think through the chat template (enable_thinking). Sampling follows the OpenBMB recommendation: chat = no-think (temp 0.7), coding = think (temp 0.9), top_p 0.95 in both. --jinja is mandatory (chat template + XML tool-call parsing). For tool calling, SGLang/llama.cpp with the correct parser is recommended.
profile_notes.minimax-01.yaml: MiniMax-Text-01 is a 456B-A45.9B MoE hybrid with Lightning Attention recurrent layers and one full-attention layer per eight blocks; MiniMax-M1 uses the same llama.cpp minimax-01 architecture. Native support landed in llama.cpp b10437. AutoTuner counts recurrent-layer boolean arrays, sizes KV only for full-attention layers, and uses expert-aware placement. The model is far larger than ordinary laptop memory even when quantized; small local systems require a heavily quantized split and substantial system RAM.
profile_notes.minimax-m2.yaml: MiniMax-M2 is a sparse-MoE model (154 experts, 8 active) tuned for agentic coding and tool use. Native context is 192k (clamped to GGUF native). The build in the tree is the REAP-pruned 139B-A10B variant — same arch tag and sampler recommendation as the full model, just fewer experts, so it shares this profile. Recommended samplers (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 40) follow MiniMaxAI's published defaults; min_p 0.02 trims the routing tail to curb repetition on the pruned weights. As a large MoE it relies on AutoTuner's capacity-fill spread to pack both GPUs with expert layers; everything else (n-cpu-moe, tensor-split, ctx) is derived automatically.
profile_notes.minimax-m3.yaml: MiniMax-M3 is a native multimodal 428B-A23B MoE with MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) and 1M context. Use llama.cpp b10142 or newer for the text, MSA, vision, and specialized tool-call path. Vision additionally requires an M3 mmproj. Use an MSA-aware GGUF conversion that retains every blk.N.index_q_proj/index_k_proj tensor; older dense-fallback GGUFs are not equivalent. Flash Attention is required for the intended sparse path; unsupported no-FA/unified-KV multi-sequence modes can fall back to dense attention and lose the 1M-context efficiency. Released weights do not contain the advertised MTP modules, so AutoTuner keeps conservative draftless speculation. Official sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95; other sampler fields are inherited from GGUF metadata.
profile_notes.ministral.yaml: Ministral 3 (3B/8B/14B), Mistral's edge family, all with vision (mmproj). The 14B Reasoning variant is comparable to Mistral Small 3.2 24B in reasoning benchmarks (85% AIME '25). The architecture shares RoPE scaling with Devstral Small 2 / Llama 4. Apache 2.0. Chat profile = Reasoning variant (temp 1.0, Mistral recommendation). The coding profile also suits the Instruct variants (temp ~0.1). Note: the pattern matches all variants; for Instruct models simply use coding mode for chat as well, or override via CLI: -- --temp 0.0
profile_notes.mistral-medium.yaml: Mistral Medium 3.5 (128B dense, multimodal text+image, 29 April 2026) is Mistral's first unified model, replacing Medium 3.1, Magistral AND Devstral 2 in one (Mistral itself: "supersedes all our previous coding models, namely Devstral, across all benchmarks"). Hybrid reasoning with per-request configurable reasoning_effort (none/high). Modified MIT License. Vibe CLI (Mistral's coding agent) now runs on Medium 3.5 instead of Devstral 2. Locally: ~64 GB RAM for UD-Q4_K_XL via llama.cpp. Chat profile = Mistral's default (temp 0.7, works for both reasoning modes). Coding profile = more deterministic (temp 0.2) for agentic code tasks. Enable reasoning mode via: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"high"}'. IMPORTANT: use GGUFs from 1 May 2026 or newer; earlier versions had a YaRN bug (mscale_all_dim) that ruined long-context performance (Mistral itself confirmed that the original Transformers config had a long-context performance bug). At Unsloth the fixed build is called, for example, UD-Q4_K_XL.
profile_notes.mistral-small-3.yaml: Dense 24B Mistral Small 3.1/3.2 instruction models with 128k context and Pixtral vision. Mistral recommends temperature 0.15 and a tailored system prompt. Current llama.cpp uses the mistral3 text architecture and requires a matching mmproj for image input; for Mistral Small 3.1 MTMD recommends the mistral-v7 chat template when a converted checkpoint does not embed it.
profile_notes.muse-glimmer.yaml: Meta Muse Glimmer 30B is a dense multimodal local-agent model with a separate perception mmproj, 131k context, interleaved reasoning/tool use, and an optional DFlash block drafter. It requires llama.cpp b10353 or newer. Official sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64 in both chat and agentic coding. Keep reasoning history for multi-turn tool workflows. Reasoning strength is controlled in the system prompt with "Reasoning strength: low|medium|high|xhigh". The Q4 model plus mmproj, KV cache, and drafter targets a 24-32 GB device; on this dual-AMD system benchmark the optional drafter because Vulkan overhead can offset gains.
profile_notes.nanbeige-4_2.yaml: Compact 3B non-embedding-parameter looped Transformer for reasoning, coding, agents, and XML tool calls. The model card advertises 262,144 context and recommends temp 0.6/top-p 0.95/top-k 20 for reasoning and temp 1.0 for agent use. Preserved thinking is useful for multi-turn tools; disable it manually when minimizing KV history matters more than continuity.
profile_notes.nemotron-3-nano-omni.yaml: Hybrid Mamba2-Transformer MoE, 30B total / ~3B active. Multimodal: text + image + audio + video (via mmproj). Reasoning variant with native <think>/</think> tokens (12/13). Chat profile = NVIDIA's official reasoning recommendation (temp 0.6). The coding profile is more deterministic (temp 0.2) for stable code output. CAUTION: do NOT use with CUDA 13.2; it produces gibberish output. NVIDIA is working on a fix; until then use CUDA 12.9 or 13.0. Tip: to force or disable thinking explicitly, append at start: -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true}' or -- --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
profile_notes.nemotron-3-puzzle.yaml: Text-only 75.3B-total/9.3B-active compression of Nemotron 3 Super with the same 88-block Mamba-2/latent-MoE/attention layout, integrated multi-token prediction, and up to 1,048,576 context (262,144 default). Puzzle prunes expert channels per layer (expert FFN widths 1280-2688), routes 4 to 18 experts depending on the layer, and shrinks the Mamba state from 128 to 96 channels. The profile requires llama.cpp b10786 because that build first reads the per-layer expert arrays; AutoTuner refuses older binaries before launch instead of letting tensor creation abort. Sampling, thinking control, and MTP settings follow the Super profile.
profile_notes.nemotron-3-super.yaml: Text-only 120B-total/12B-active Mamba-2 + latent-MoE + attention hybrid (88 blocks: 40 Mamba, 40 MoE, 8 attention) with integrated multi-token prediction and up to 1,048,576 context; NVIDIA deploys 262,144 by default. Official sampling is temp 1.0/top-p 0.95 for every task. Thinking is controlled through the chat template (enable_thinking, low_effort, and a reasoning budget), which AutoTuner drives with its reasoning dropdown and --reasoning-budget. The profile enables the integrated MTP head with three draft tokens as NVIDIA recommends and keeps MTP-compatible n-gram speculation. At roughly 60 GB in Q4 this is a two-GPU or CPU-expert-offload workstation model, not a 16 GB single-card checkpoint.
profile_notes.nemotron-3_5.yaml: Text-only 30B-total/3B-active Mamba-2 + attention + MoE hybrid with one integrated MTP layer and up to 1,048,576 context. NVIDIA's official sampling is temp 1.0/top-p 0.95. Mainline b10665 adds its DSpark sidecar contract; AutoTuner uses n-max 7 and p-min 0.0 so confidence-head-free releases do not abort. The official local llama.cpp example starts around 40,960 context; larger windows remain subject to measured KV/recurrent/runtime capacity.
profile_notes.ornith-1_5.yaml: Ornith 1.5 is a Qwen3.5-based reasoning/tool-calling family with 256k native context and validated YaRN extension to about 1M. Official general sampling is temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 (presence 1.5), while precise coding uses temp 0.6 and presence 0.0. AutoTuner keeps presence at 0.0 in both modes so OpenAI-style tool JSON remains stable; pure chat users can override it to 1.5. Filename-only matching avoids stealing opaque qwen35/qwen35moe re-quants from the generic Qwen profile. The older Ornith 1.0 profile remains unchanged.
profile_notes.ornith.yaml: Ornith 1.0 (DeepReinforce, June 2026, MIT): self-improving model family for agentic coding, post-trained on a Qwen 3.5 base. The GGUF architecture is "qwen35" (9B/31B dense) or "qwen35moe" (35B-A3B / 397B-A17B MoE), exactly the Qwen3.5/3.6 hybrid family (GatedDeltaNet + full attention); the scanner counts the KV cache correctly through recurrent_layers. This profile matches only by the filename pattern ("ornith"); re-quants without "ornith" in the name correctly land at qwen3_5-3_6.yaml. Reasoning model: the answer opens with <think>...</think> by default. Set `--jinja` as an extra arg at start so that the <think> block is cleanly separated into the reasoning_content field and <tool_call> blocks are parsed as OpenAI-style tool_calls (Ornith is primarily a tool-calling agent): -- --jinja. Sampling: uniformly temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 for chat AND coding (Ornith recommendation); temp=1.0 is only the benchmark reproduction value (-- --temp 1.0). Unlike generic Qwen3.5 (chat temp=1.0), which is the reason for this separate profile despite the identical architecture. Tip: the 9B dense model is suitable as an external draft model (Path A) for the 35B MoE; the GGUFs themselves ship no integrated MTP head.
profile_notes.paddleocr-vl.yaml: Compact 0.9B multilingual document VLM (109 languages), supported by llama.cpp's paddleocr text architecture and MTMD projector path. Official element prompts are "OCR:", "Table Recognition:", "Formula Recognition:", and "Chart Recognition:"; generation is deterministic. AutoTuner attaches a compatible sibling mmproj when present. This exposes element recognition via llama-server; it does not reproduce PaddleOCR's separate full page-layout pipeline or post-processing stages.
profile_notes.qwen-agentworld.yaml: Alibaba Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B: the first language world model (CPT+SFT+RL on environment simulation across 7 domains: MCP/tool, search, terminal, SWE, Android, web, OS), Apache-2.0. NO separate architecture: it is Qwen3.5-35B-A3B further trained, general.architecture "qwen35moe" (hybrid GatedDeltaNet + attention, 256 experts / 8+1, native 262k context). Separate profile by filename pattern "agentworld" (NO arch_fallback, because the architecture is identical to regular Qwen3.5/3.6-A3B and a duplicate qwen35moe fallback would become order-dependent), because the AgentWorld sampling recommendation (temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=20 in BOTH modes) deliberately differs from the generic Qwen3.5 coder/chat settings (temp 1.0 thinking): a world model should simulate consistent, factual state transitions. Thinking mode by default (<think>), qwen3 reasoning parser, --jinja mandatory. Qwen advises >=128k context (on OOM quantise the KV cache instead of lowering context below 128k); recommended output length 32k. Domain-specific system prompts live in the GitHub repository (prompts/); AgentWorld as an environment simulator needs these system prompts to deliver meaningful observations. With 3B active plus --n-cpu-moe it runs well on a 32 GB card; it runs on mainline llama-server (no fork). Regular Qwen3.5/3.6 models remain covered by qwen3_5-3_6.yaml.
profile_notes.qwen2_5-3.yaml: Excellent all-round model. The coding profile runs at temp=0.2 (vs. 0.7 chat); the Coder variants can also be run at an even lower temperature (0.1). Selectable through the GUI mode. Also catches Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (architecture qwen3moe) and Qwen3-Coder-Next (architecture qwen3next) through the pattern "qwen3-coder". Both have 256k native context, hence max_context 262144 (previously wrongly capped at 131072). Qwen3-Coder-Next is a hybrid (Gated DeltaNet + gated attention) and needs a current llama.cpp version with the DeltaNet operators, present on b9310. Note: Qwen3-Coder-Instruct is a pure instruct model without thinking; Alibaba recommends temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 for it (chat mode at 0.7/0.9 is close). For deterministic code editing use coding mode (temp 0.2).
profile_notes.qwen3-vl.yaml: Alibaba Qwen3-VL: vision-language models, dense (2B/4B/8B/32B) and MoE (30B-A3B / 235B-A22B), Instruct + Thinking, architecture "qwen3vl" or "qwen3vlmoe" (both in llama.cpp mainline). Needs an mmproj file for the vision encoder; assign it as mmproj in the GUI; without mmproj only the text path runs. Sampling distinguishes Instruct (chat: temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8) and Thinking (coding: temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95), analogous to Qwen3.5/3.6. presence_penalty is set to 0.0 instead of Qwen's 1.5 because 1.5 causes tool-calling loops; for pure image description without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`. Note: on Vulkan/ROCm it has been reported that Qwen3-VL does not fully utilise the GPU (~80%) and is somewhat slower than the plain Qwen3 text model (llama.cpp #16895); not a fault of this profile.
profile_notes.qwen3_5-3_6.yaml: Qwen3.5 (February 2026) and Qwen3.6 (April 2026) are thinking-by-default multimodal models with 256k native context (extendable to 1.01M via YaRN). The original Qwen3 has only 32k and is automatically limited through the GGUF native_context. The chat profile corresponds to the official thinking setup; the coding profile mirrors the official QwenClawBench setting (temp=0.6). presence_penalty is set to 0.0 here instead of the official Qwen recommendation of 1.5 because 1.5 reproducibly causes tool-calling loops (structured output needs repeated tokens, which a high presence_penalty punishes). For pure chat without tools: `-- --presence-penalty 1.5`. New in Qwen3.6: the `preserve_thinking` API flag keeps thinking content across multi-turn conversations for better agentic consistency. Tip: `--jinja` as an extra arg at start enables the clean separation of <think> blocks into the reasoning_content API field (instead of leaving them inline in content): -- --jinja
profile_notes.qwen3_8.yaml: Qwen3.8-27B is a dense native vision-language model with optional thinking; Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is a text-only MoE (2.4T total, 95B active) whose thinking mode cannot be disabled. Both use a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/full-attention layout, preserve historical reasoning by default, and support reasoning_effort values xhigh (default), medium, and low. The profile therefore enables Jinja and preserved reasoning and uses the official thinking defaults in both AutoTuner modes. Only the 27B model supports non-thinking inference; when selecting it manually, use enable_thinking=false together with temp 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty 1.5, and repeat_penalty 1.0. Avoid that high presence penalty for repetitive tool-call JSON if it causes loops. Vision requires a matching 27B mmproj once a GGUF conversion publishes one. External Qwen3.8 DFlash2 sidecars require mainline b10658+ (older builds only have the 58-tensor DFlash graph). AutoTuner detects that mismatch before launch and derives n-max 7 from the sidecar's block_size=8 metadata. The 2.4T checkpoint is datacenter-scale and not realistically runnable on a workstation, even with aggressive quantization and CPU expert offload.
profile_notes.qwen3_8_flash_next.yaml: Dedicated profile for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUFs declaring qwen4exp. Mainline llama.cpp added the loader in b10660 and AutoTuner's QSA graph-memory safety contract was measured on b10666. AutoTuner requires b10737+ because the follow-up QSA sequence-copy, block-keying, multimodal-input, and CUDA-abort fixes in PR #27941 are required for correct serving. The model has 48 hybrid MoE blocks, 512 experts with 10 active, full attention every fourth block (12 normal KV layers), an additional QSA indexer cache, and 262,144 native context. Its PLE per-layer n-gram embedding table is a giant read-lazy host mapping rather than splittable layer weight; AutoTuner sizes the full file mapping separately from its active-row residency and defaults this profile to Safe/ubatch 64. Balanced/Throughput remain available at ubatch 128/256 because the QSA graph grows with context x ubatch. PLE is not advertised as generic draft-mtp.
profile_notes.seed-oss.yaml: ByteDance Seed-OSS-36B-Instruct: dense 36B reasoning/agentic model, Apache-2.0, native 512k context, architecture "seed_oss". Special feature: a controllable thinking budget (CoT length freely selectable, 512 tokens to unlimited); on hard tasks (AIME, LiveCodeBench) the score rises with a larger budget. Sampling follows the ByteDance recommendation temp=1.1 (!) / top_p=0.95 in chat; the high temperature is the vendor's intention; the coding profile is somewhat more conservative (temp 1.0 / top_p 0.8, compare Taubench 1.0/0.7). --jinja for the thinking template. Dense, so no MoE offload; quantised it fits well on a 32 GB card.
profile_notes.shieldstral.yaml: Mistral Shieldstral 1.0 3B is a policy-adaptive multimodal safety CLASSIFIER, not a conversational assistant. It is based on Ministral 3 and runs in current llama.cpp after Mistral-format conversion. Text moderation needs only the model GGUF; image moderation also needs the Pixtral mmproj. Use a single yes/no policy question per request. The client should request max_tokens=1 with logprobs/top_logprobs and derive the normalized yes/no score; that response-side setting is not a llama-server launch flag and therefore cannot be encoded in this YAML. Official inference uses greedy temperature 0.0. Although the base architecture exposes 256k RoPE, the model card recommends the 32k training range.
profile_notes.smollm3.yaml: HuggingFace SmolLM3-3B: dense 3B model, Apache-2.0, architecture "smollm3", dual-mode reasoning (think/no-think via /think or /no_think in the chat template), native 64k context (128k via YaRN). Sampling follows the HF card temp=0.6 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=40; coding slightly more deterministic. --jinja for template + reasoning separation. Small and fast; good as a draft model or for light edge workloads.
profile_notes.step35.yaml: StepFun Step 3.5 Flash (text) + Step 3.7 Flash (VLM, +image/video), both sparse MoE ~196-198B total / ~11B active, 3:1 SWA/full attention, MTP-3, 256k context. Both load under architecture "step35". SIZE WARNING: a ~196-198B MoE far exceeds this system's 48 GB (VRAM+RAM); realistically it runs only with massive CPU MoE offload and slow generation, or not at all. The profile exists for correctness/the future. Reasoning levels (low/medium/high) are controlled via the chat template/API. draft_max is set to 3 (native MTP-3 depth); possibly unstable on Vulkan, then reduce to 2 in the Expert panel. Step-3.7-Flash needs a separate mmproj file for vision. `--jinja` enables clean reasoning separation: -- --jinja
profile_notes.trinity-afmoe.yaml: Arcee AI Trinity (AFMoE / "afmoe", AfmoeForCausalLM): attention-first MoE, in llama.cpp since b7061. Nano = 6B total / ~1B active, Mini = 26B / ~3B, each with 128 experts (8 active, 1 shared), 128k native context. NOT a Mamba hybrid: full KV cache per layer (the tuner's hybrid logic correctly does NOT apply here). This profile also covers Dolphin-X1-Trinity-Nano (dphn), the RL-uncensored retrain of Trinity-Nano: same architecture, same ChatML template, only the alignment differs. With Dolphin the system prompt controls tone and alignment (for example "You are Dolphin, a helpful, unbiased, and uncensored AI assistant."); without a system prompt the model behaves in an unspecific default. Sampling follows Arcee's official recommendation (temp 0.15 / top_k 50 / top_p 0.75 / min_p 0.06), deliberately deterministic for stable tool/structured output. Trinity-Mini can run via vLLM with the deepseek_r1 reasoning parser + hermes tool parser; under llama.cpp `--jinja` handles the template/channel separation.
profile_notes.unlimited-ocr.yaml: OCR/document model. Use AutoTuner's OCR workflow so images are normalized, PDFs are rendered page-by-page, and Word/Office files are converted through LibreOffice before they are sent to llama-server. The verified prompt is "document parsing."; "Free OCR." can return immediate EOS on Unlimited-OCR.
profile_notes.vibethinker.yaml: WeiboAI VibeThinker: dense reasoning model (3B on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, or 1.5B), MIT licence, specialised in verifiable reasoning (maths/code/STEM). Architecture "qwen2", therefore NO arch_fallback (it would otherwise catch generic Qwen2 models); matching only by filename. Sampling follows the official WeiboAI recommendation temp=1.0 / top_p=0.95 / top_k=-1 in BOTH modes: a lower temperature demonstrably worsens reasoning quality here; the model is not trained for other temperature regimes. <think> block: parse downstream. Not a general-purpose model; take a larger model for broad world knowledge.
